Issued at 350 AM EDT Wed Sep 2 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Southwesterly flow aloft across much of the CONUS...from the Pacific 
to the Upper Midwest. PV maxima embedded in the flow over the 
Dakotas...upper low spinning to our northeast over central Ontario 
and filling as it does so...with more or less zonal flow aloft over 
the Upper Great Lakes between this an southern stream ridge axis 
still centered over the Mid MS Valley. We continue to tap both 
Pacific moisture, and a bit of Gulf moisture, though right now, most 
of the latter is focused near "Edouard" over southern TX... but 
still, pwats at or above 1.5 in in the region, with swath of 2+in 
pwats along deformation axis from the central Plains to SW MI and 
some weaker stability in place, particularly near Neb/SD/IA, where 
convection is blossoming as of 4z. SW-ly nocturnal LLJ is nosing 
into this area as well, further favoring the idea of convection 
there. Some thunderstorms have tracked across Whitefish Bay toward 
Soo Canada thus far, though, along the portion of the 
front/baroclinic zone associated with the northern stream upper low 
(dewpoints drop back into the 50s and 60s behind this...as opposed 
to the 70s ahead of it, even at 4z). Evening convection that 
developed on the lake breeze in NE Lower still tracking eastward 
across central Lake Huron at 4z, too...and airmass here in Lower MI 
remains juicy and somewhat juiced, instability-wise, though some 
radiational cooling is resulting in the usual near-surface nocturnal 
inversion and some CINH. 

Expect upstream baroclinic zone/convection to buckle northeastward, 
with plume of deeper moisture likely to advect into the region 
along/ahead of the boundary this morning. Attm, appears some 
semblance of a cold front may drape into the area this 
evening/tonight as the cooler airmass to our north scrapes the area. 
In the meantime...this will leave the Upper Midwest in a col region 
tonight into Thursday, favorable for an area of renewed moisture 
pooling/frontogenesis...particularly as upstream system begins to 
cross the Plains. Will expect a return to juicy conditions Thursday 
into Friday as deep moisture focuses near and north of a 
boundary/warm front likely stretching from the Northern Plains into 
southern MI. Ridge axis appears to build to our west across the 
Upper MS Valley going into the weekend, and will need to keep an eye 
out for some warm advection activity...though we may get in on some 
ridging by later in the weekend as a northern stream system passes 
across north/central Canada and scrapes off the top of the ridge. 
Guidance continues to struggle with how this will evolve, though 
currently, solutions seem to be leaning toward the ridge axis 
prevailing over the Great Lakes, shunting the aforementioned 
northern stream system to our north...as troughing over the PacNW 
begins to eject early next week. This idea would support warm and 
unsettled weather continuing into at least the middle of next week, 
with potential for troughing to generally prevail over the western 
US/West Coast beyond this. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/storms today/tonight... upstream convective complexes (noting a 
nice bow echo over southern MN at 5z) may try to hold together and 
track into our area through the remainder of the morning; think the 
better chance for more organized storms is just to our south as 
usual, though it's not out of the question it remains further north, 
given a more or less zonal thickness gradient into the region, and a 
SW flow component that may offset Coriolis effects that would 
otherwise veer it south. At the very least...we could/should end up 
in the stratiform portion of whatever globs of convection track 
eastward this morning. Worth noting that there is still some 
semblance of a boundary draped across the Straits region attm (6z) 
with lower dewpoints north and dewpoints still solidly in the 70s 
across most of northern Lower (most of Lower MI as a whole, for that 
matter), and this could serve to focus some additional development 
this morning further north than anticipated, across the Tip of the 
Mitt region and perhaps the EUP....noting there are some signals for 
gravity waves out there this morning, too, to further throw a 
convective wrench into things. Best shot for any stronger storms 
this morning through midday would likely be near and south of M-72. 
Think this area could also be worth keeping an eye on through the 
afternoon, particularly if there is enough diurnal heating across 
the Saginaw Bay region early in the day (predicated on not too much 
cloud cover) to result in some improved instability there. This is 
largely where the Day 1 marginal risk for severe weather is located 
(generally near and south of a line from Alpena/Ossineke to 
Frankfort/Arcadia), and this seems like a reasonable idea. Guidance 
soundings suggest there is a chance the atmosphere recovers and 
destabilizes again this afternoon, especially in this regio
